title: King Oliver and Armstrong leaving: the second trumpet tradition
summary: Barker says there was no bitterness when Armstrong left Joe Oliver, explaining the New Orleans tradition of a second trumpet.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Did you know Papa Joe Oliver?
Yes, I knew Joe Oliver. Do you think, I mean, some people,

some people have indicated that he really wanted Louis to stay with him in Chicago when Louis left and went to New York, and that I think Lil Armstrong, his wife, his second wife, sort of had an influence on his leaving the band. Do you think there was any bitterness on Joe's part when Louis left to go to Chicago?

Oh, that's not no bitterness. I don't think there was no, there was no bitterness, but it was a sort of a, a loss to Joe because there was a tradition in New Orleans to have two trumpets in the band. Papa Celestine had two, at one time, Manny Perez had two, first and second trumpet. And, uh, other bands around had two trumpets, and you played second. And it was guys, it's just like baseball, a second string catcher, you dig, more than one pitcher, and, uh, or more than one quarterback in a, a football team. It was a thing. And, uh, like, Joe was up in age, like most trumpets who had gotten age, up in age, well, they didn't have the fire, or they didn't want to blow themselves to death, so they brought in a youngster and let him blow a second, like, Bunk Johnson lots of times sat in with Bolden, see? Uh, Ricard Alexis and, uh, Moeys Durant sat in with Manuel, Manuel Perez. Shots, Madison sat in with Papa Celestan. You got it? It was a tradition. When, when, when, when, when Lurie left, Joe Oliver imported Lee Collins. He tried to get Kid Rene. Younger trumpet players to come and play the second. I'm, you know, I'm the boss, but here's somebody, you know, it was a thing. It was a fraternal thing about him, you know, two peas in a pod, and I get another, like a relief. But in other words, you could make your name with a big band. To, it was to your advantage. To be playing in a, at a band, leader, which was a band, with a leader who was tenant to business, had an organized band in the top spot in New Orleans or playing for the top people. To play in a band, it was constantly an evolution of going up a step high, graduating.
there was some, a feeling, I guess, you know, he was glad to, he was sorry to leave Louie, because he and Louie was the famous duets they did, you dig?
